steps.notes: Gold + independent impl pass tests 1-3; test 4 raises NameError under per-test isolation (passes 4/4 only in the official shared-namespace concatenated script). Targets for tests 1-3 have degenerate all-zero filtered_image.

findings.evidence: All three numeric targets' filtered_image arrays are numerically zero: target img min/max = -3.55e-17/3.55e-17 (test 1), +-1.16e-17 (test 2), +-1.08e-17 (test 3) -- far below np.allclose's default atol=1e-8. Cause: the test input np.tile([[1,0,0,0],[0,0,0,1]], (400,200)) is exactly periodic (periods 2 and 4), so its 800x800 spectrum has peaks only at shifted-bin radii r = 0, 200.0, 447.2, 565.7; measured max in-band |F| is 1.29e-11 / 2.19e-12 / 2.28e-12 vs global max 1.6e5 for bands (20,50)/(40,80)/(80,100). Every spectral peak lies OUTSIDE every tested band, so the band-pass output is machine noise. Dynamic proof: review/work/7/step_7.1_wrong_zeros.py builds the correct mask T but performs NO Fourier transform and returns np.zeros_like(image_array) as filtered_image; assembled official-style (all 4 tests concatenated, review/work/7/official_style_wrong_zeros.py) it exits 0 -- full credit. Test 4 likewise only compares T1.sum()-T2.sum() > 0. Net effect: the entire fft2 -> mask -> ifft2 pipeline that the prompt asks to 'simulate' is completely unconstrained; only the binary annulus mask T is ever tested.
findings.suggested_fix: Add at least one test whose input has spectral energy inside the tested band (e.g., a seeded random image, a Gaussian spot, or sinusoids with spatial frequencies of radius 30-60 bins) so the frozen filtered_image target is non-trivial; or assert on the filtered image of the existing input with a band that contains the r=200 peaks (e.g., bandmin,bandmax = 150,250).

findings.evidence: Test case 4's code calls 'T1, filtered_image1 = apply_band_pass_filter(image_array, bandmin,bandmax)' BEFORE any 'image_array = ...' assignment in that test case; image_array is only defined later (for the T2 call). It executes successfully only because the official harness (SciCode/eval/scripts/test_generated_code.py lines 60-70 and eval/inspect_ai/scicode.py lines 287-300) concatenates all test cases into ONE script sharing module namespace, so image_array leaks in from test case 3. Under per-test isolation, even the official gold fails: 'python3 review/tools/steptest.py --problem 7 --step 7.1 --use-gold' -> test 4/4 FAIL, NameError: name 'image_array' is not defined (tests 1-3 PASS). Verified the official concatenated style passes 4/4 (review/work/7/official_style_gold.py, exit 0). The test case also contains a stray unused line 'frequency_threshold = 100'. Note steptest.py's docstring claims it 'mirrors the official scorer exactly' but isolates per test, so this repo's own runner mis-scores the gold on this step.
findings.suggested_fix: Make test case 4 self-contained: insert 'image_array = np.tile(matrix, (400, 200))' immediately after the first 'matrix = ...' line (before the T1 call), and delete the unused 'frequency_threshold = 100' line. No h5 change needed (target stays True).

findings.evidence: step_background says 'The filter takes input image in size of [m,n] and the frequency threshold. Ouput the nxn array as the filtered image' -- output described as n x n while input is m x n, and 'the frequency threshold' (singular) contradicts the two thresholds bandmin/bandmax in the header. All tests use a square 800x800 image and the header/docstring correctly describe two band edges and 2D outputs, so no scoring impact; cosmetic inconsistency only.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword background to 'Output the m x n arrays (mask and filtered image)' and 'the frequency band edges (bandmin, bandmax)'.

overall_assessment: Solvable and the intended conventions (FFT-bin radius from the fftshift DC bin at (m//2,n//2); strictly exclusive band edges, which the prompt states explicitly) are inferable; gold and an independent implementation pass the official harness. However the tests only constrain the binary annulus mask T: every numeric target's filtered_image is degenerate machine-noise zero because all spectral peaks of the periodic test input lie outside the tested bands, so an implementation that skips the Fourier pipeline entirely scores full credit (verified). Additionally test case 4 is not self-contained (NameError on image_array) and passes only via cross-test namespace leakage in the official concatenated script; any per-test-isolated harness, including this repo's steptest, fails even the gold on it. Fair to score correct solutions as-is, but weak against wrong ones and fragile to harness changes.
